freshly_checked_applications.title: Finite decomposition/completion and inertia residue quotient, with compatible restrictions
freshly_checked_applications.author: J. S. Milne

theorem_locators.scope: Finite Galois extension of complete discretely valued fields with separable residue extension: quotient by inertia is the residue Galois group.
Finite Galois extension of number fields: the chosen decomposition group is the Galois group of the corresponding completions.
Restriction in a finite Galois tower maps the chosen decomposition group onto that of the Galois subextension.

hypotheses_checked: The original field is a number field and Omega its algebraic closure; the inverse system consists only of finite Galois subextensions.
The valuation lies over an original finite prime; corresponding completions are complete discretely valued number-field completions.
Their residue fields are finite and therefore perfect, and every finite residue extension is separable.
In each transition the lower finite subextension is Galois, so the fixing subgroup is normal as required in Proposition 8.13(b).
The source Dec is the valuation stabilizer and source Ine acts trivially on its residue field; these are the same definitions used by the finite theorem.
freshly_checked_applications.human_proof_use: CFO11 uses only these finite facts; it proves the absolute inverse-limit quotient, residue algebraic-closure argument and Frobenius normalization. CFO14 proves the entire cocycle count independently.
freshly_checked_applications.excluded_scope: No local/global duality, local class-field-theory LocCFT, or ordinary automorphic existence is certified by this application.
freshly_checked_applications.errata_checked: Checked the author errata. The proof never treats an infinite algebraic extension as a complete DVR. The finite theorem is used as stated; the absolute passage is written in CFO11.

note: Only the finite Milne decomposition/inertia facts are imported; CFO proves the absolute passage. No ordinary/control, LocCFT, global-duality or initial analytic producer is silently imported.
